players: 8-10 (numbers below are for 8; '+1/+2' says what to add)
equipment: Cones (4 colours) to mark the lanes
focus: In possession: two players in each lane, and when the full-back comes inside, the inside mid (8) goes out wide
objectives: Every player can name the 5 lanes and checks the 'two per lane' picture before receiving
Full-back inverts into the half-space and the 8 drifts wide at the same moment, creating a 2v1 on their centre mid
Find the free player (the 8 out wide, or the 6 into the 8) within 2 passes of the CB receiving
key_messages: "Two in a lane" - never three, never zero
"Who's free?" - check your shoulder before the ball arrives
"Open up" - receive on the open body, ready to play forward

blocks.title: Rondo 5+1 v 2: find the pivot

diagram.caption: 5 outside + 1 pivot (6) keep the ball from 2 pressers. A pass through the pressers into the pivot = 1 point.

blocks.setup: One 18x18m grid. 8 players: 5 outside, 1 pivot in the middle, 2 pressers. 9 players: add a second pivot (5+2 v 2). 10 players: add a third presser (5+2 v 3).
how: Outside players keep the ball, max 2 touches.
Pass through the pressers into the pivot = 1 point; pivot plays out to a different side = 2 points.
Pressers win it: the player who lost it swaps in.
Last 3 minutes: pivot must receive and turn in one action (open body).
blocks.link_to_theme: The pivot is the free player between the lines. It starts the session's habit: who's free, and can I find them?
coaching_points: Pivot moves into the gap between the 2 pressers, not behind one of them
Outside players receive on the open stick side, body side-on so they can see the pivot and the next outside player
Pivot checks shoulder before the ball arrives so the first touch goes away from pressure
blocks.activity_notes: Everyone is in the grid: no queues at 8, 9 or 10.

blocks.title: FB in, 8 out: the inversion pattern (one-side unit)

diagram.caption: Left side of the pitch: wide lane, half-space, centre. As LCB receives, LB steps inside and the 8 drifts wide. LCB finds the free player and the unit carries over the far line.

blocks.setup: 45x33m area (the left third of the pitch width, from the 23 to halfway) with 3 lanes coned. 8 players: blue RCB, LCB, LB, 6, 8, LW + red W and CM. 9: add a blue 9 high in the centre. 10: add a red FB who marks the LW.
how: RCB plays across to LCB. As the ball travels, LB steps inside into the half-space and the 8 drifts out to the wide lane.
Pattern A: LCB to 6, 6 opens up and plays out to the 8 wide, 8 carries over the far line.
Pattern B: LCB into LB on the back foot (open body), one-touch set to the 6, 6 plays the diagonal into the 8.
First 6 minutes unopposed at 70%, then the red W and CM go live at 50% and the LCB must pick the right pattern.
Rotate 2 blue players into red every 4 reps. Last 8 minutes: flip the cones and do it on the right side.
blocks.link_to_theme: The core rotation of the whole programme. All of it happens on one side of the pitch, so a unit of 6 learns it exactly as the full team will use it.
coaching_points: Timing: LB and 8 move as the ball travels to the LCB, not after the LCB has received
LB receives in the half-space with an open body (shoulders facing the far side) so they can play forward or set
8 arrives wide on the blind side of their winger, who is watching the ball
LCB: if the W blocks the line to the LB, the 8 wide is the free player - play it early
questions: Their winger followed our LB inside: who is free now?
Why does the 8 have to go wide when the LB comes in?
progressions: Red CM jumps to whoever receives, live
regressions: Red players passive (stick only, no tackling)
Coach calls 'A' or 'B' to choose the pattern
blocks.activity_notes: All 8-10 involved every rep. Reps reset from the RCB every 15-20 seconds, so there's no standing about.

blocks.title: Lane game 5v3: build out with two per lane

diagram.caption: Blue 5 build from the start line and score by dribbling over the end line. Red 3 press and counter into 2 mini goals. Max 2 blue per lane.

blocks.setup: Same 45x33m, 3-lane area. 8 players: blue 5 (LCB, LB, 6, 8, LW) v red 3 (W, CM, FB). 9: add a red 4th (second CM) for 5v4. 10: add a blue 9 and a red CB (6v4). Swap 3 blue into red every 4 minutes.
how: Coach feeds the LCB on the start line.
Blue score 1 by dribbling over the end line; 2 if the move used the FB-in/8-out rotation.
Rule: max 2 blue in any lane when a pass is played - coach shouts 'Three!' and red get the ball.
Red win it: 6 seconds to score in either mini goal behind the LCB.
blocks.link_to_theme: Takes the pattern into a live build-out where the two-per-lane rule is enforced and rewarded.
coaching_points: Scan the lane picture before you receive: who has left my lane, who do I need to replace?
Free player usually appears on the blind side of their winger
Ball speed: 2 touches maximum while we have the 2v1 on their CM
If the lane is blocked, recycle to the LCB and restart the picture
questions: When our LB stepped in, what did their CM have to decide?
progressions: Red go +1 so blue lose the spare player
regressions: Red CM must stay in the centre lane
Remove the lane turnover rule and just reward rotations
blocks.activity_notes: Everyone plays. Coach has 10 balls at the start line for instant restarts; rest is the 5-10 seconds between reps.

step.space: Narrow to 28m if blue find it too easy
step.people: Fittest players go red - they do the most running

blocks.title: 4v4 (+ floaters): lane bonus game

diagram.caption: 4v4 across 3 lanes with 2 mini goals each end. In your own half, max 2 per lane. Goal from a FB-in/8-out rotation = 2.

blocks.setup: 50x40m (across the 23 to halfway), 3 lanes coned, 2 mini goals at each end. 8 players: 4v4 (CB, FB, 8, W each). 9: 1 neutral floater for the team in possession. 10: 2 floaters, or 5v5 adding a 6.
how: Every restart is a pass from the team's CB on their own goal line, so we build every time.
In your own half, max 2 per lane: free hit to the other team if broken.
Goal from a move that included the FB-in/8-out rotation = 2.
Coach freezes play once every 4 minutes to show a good or missed lane picture (30 seconds max).
blocks.link_to_theme: Same rule, game tempo: both teams live and transitions happening.
coaching_points: Re-form the lane picture quickly after winning the ball
The 8 who goes wide must be ready to receive and drive, not just stand there
Rest-defence: while the FB is inside, the CB stays connected for the counter
progressions: Lane rule applies across the whole area
regressions: Add a floater even at 8 (coach plays)
Remove the lane rule and keep the bonus
blocks.activity_notes: Everyone plays. Play 4 x 4-minute games with 1 minute rest; ball-stocks behind each goal.

blocks.title: 4v4 / 5v5 on the half pitch: two per lane
blocks.setup: Half pitch (halfway to the back line), 2 mini goals at halfway and the full goal at the other end (or 2 mini goals if no GK). 4v4, 4v4+1 or 5v5. Swap ends and bibs at 10 minutes.
how: Normal game, no conditions except the focus.
Focus: every time a team builds from the back, check the picture - two in each lane on the ball side.
Coach counts how many FB-in/8-out rotations each team completes.
coaching_points: Look for the 2v1 on their centre mid
Timing of the rotation: as the pass travels
Celebrate finding the free player, not only goals
questions: How many times did we find the 8 out wide? What stopped it when it didn't work?

safety: Shin guards and gum shields for all
No raised hits in blocks 1-4 (small areas)
If a GK trains, they must be fully kitted before going in goal
reflection_prompts: Did players move as the ball travelled, or after it arrived?
Which side (left or right) found the rotation more naturally?
Who needs one-to-one video on their lane positioning before Week 2?
